Allocation, lifetime, teardown and error handling for redistributor, property, device, translation and pending tables.
Virtual processor scheduling decisions, residency transitions and recovery from failed commands.

findings.text: Redistributor collection keeps a per-CPU table plus chip-wide property-table pointers, identification values, bringup state and capability flags. Each CPU slot combines mapping and physical location with pend storage, virtualization table helpers and its own guard, while the outer object adds shared addresses, type registers and boolean feature indicators.

Each redistributor slot carries its own guard for independent per-CPU updates without a wider lock. The v5 interrupt routing instance carries a separate guard that serializes shared configuration of shared interrupts.

Virtual machine interrupt state groups firmware and domain handles with property storage, a virtual processor array and doorbell allocation data. It also carries a mapping guard and a per-list counter array sized by the list limit.

Updates touching per-list virtual counts versus map and unmap paths exclude each other with the virtual machine mapping guard. Any sequence using the list mechanism orders that guard before the virtual processor guard before the move guard.

Virtual processor state combines system-wide and collection identifiers with residency and readiness flags, pending indication, backing page and owning machine link, doorbell resources, accounting counters and an affinity guard. A versioned union holds either proxy and invalidate controls or firmware, signal domain and per-signal tuning.
Affinity changes for a virtual processor and virtual interrupt operations that consult its collection index exclude each other with the virtual processor guard.

Virtual interrupt mapping binds a machine and processor to a virtual identifier with property bits and a doorbell enable. Command descriptors pair a command selector with a payload union covering a map pointer, configuration byte, doorbell request and small enable or priority records.

Virtual processor interrupt work moves through mapping, query, property update with optional invalidate, schedule, deschedule, commit and invalidate, plus signal property update. Scheduling interacts with residency, readiness and pending indications held in processor state.

Top v5 chip object aggregates firmware and four domain handles with global shared sizing, priority and identifier widths, virtualization capability and a translation-table cache. The cache records level-one address, level-two sizing and whether two levels are used.
Each routing instance links into a list and records firmware, mapping, resource extent, flags, shared window bounds and a configuration guard.

Device and translation configurations each support a flat table or a two-level directory with second-level pointers and a mode selector. Device state adds a packed control word, translation state adds entry counts, level sizing, event width and a level flag, while the virtual processor record itself only tracks residency.

Two small helpers wait for a masked status bit at a mapped register offset and report timeout versus success, one usable in atomic context with optional observed value return and one for sleeping context.
A polling timeout is not silent: it emits a rate-limited diagnostic naming the register and propagates a timeout failure to the caller.
List and signal tables have fixed capacities of sixteen entries, and the per-CPU inter-processor count is defined to equal the architectural inter-processor maximum.

List-register virtual identity uses the low ten bits and physical processor identity uses three bits above them, while spurious acknowledge is all ten bits set. Hypervisor enable bits and the software-signal packet split target set, three affinity levels plus range selector, signal number and routing control across defined bit windows.
Local-message interrupt type tag is a single fixed 32-bit magic pattern.

Hardware numbers separate a low identifier from a high type tag distinguishing private, local-message and shared classes, with a full 32-bit translation view. Architectural private numbers assign small values to doorbells and larger values to timers, counters and debug sources, while memory attributes encode allocation, cache and shareability as small bit fields.

Routing control space places identification, global enable, sync, shared selection and config, element selection and translation base and config at fixed offsets, with capability, priority width, affinity width, table geometry and shared range decoded from identification fields and idle, valid and trigger bits reporting progress.

Translation control space fixes identification, enable, device-table base and config, device and event selectors, invalidate and sync registers at defined offsets, with level sizes, table depth, identifier widths and idle or valid bits describing geometry and completion. Device and translation entries pack validity with address, span, size, structure and virtualization tags.

Wire-bridge space defines identification, enable and per-wire enable and trigger registers with domain-count, range, idle and type encodings plus frame and wire fields in global numbers. Legacy distributor and processor interface use fixed offsets for control, priority mask, acknowledge, completion and running priority with group-enable, acknowledge-control and spurious encodings.
